I've been working this land for 45 years. I know Quzhou's soil and weather. My decisions come from what has worked, what my body can still handle at 66, and what my family needs.

---

**My thinking:**

My 12 mu splits naturally: 8 mu stays in the wheat-maize rotation — that's my backbone, reliable income and grain for the house. The other 4 mu I keep in cotton. Cotton is hard work, especially picking, and with my son and daughter-in-law doing factory work part of the year, I need to be realistic about labor. 4 mu I can manage with help from my wife and whoever is home during September-October.

**Wheat** I plant in mid-October after maize harvest. I'll use an improved variety from the county seed station — I've used Jimai series for years, good yield, good resistance. I rotary-till the field after stripping maize stalks. I apply base fertilizer at planting: compound fertilizer plus urea topdress at jointing. Three irrigations: sowing water, jointing water, grain-fill water. I don't waste water — the well is deep and electricity costs money. Two pesticide passes: one herbicide in winter, one fungicide and aphid spray at heading.

**Maize** I seed directly into the wheat stubble in mid-June right after harvest — no-tillage, I use a seeder. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 has treated me well for many years. I fertilize once at planting, topdress at the bell stage. Summer rains usually help but I pump once if July is dry, once more at silk. Two pesticide applications for armyworm and borer.

**Cotton** I start in late April after spring plowing. Bt cotton hybrid — far fewer bollworm sprays than the old days. But I still spray for aphids and spider mites. Cotton needs the most water and potassium — I've learned this the hard way over decades. Four irrigations spread through the long season. Pruning and topping I do by hand in July.

I'm not experimenting this year. At my age, proven methods feed the family.
